productName: Cosori Dual-Blaze & Premium Electric Air Fryers
unitsAffected: ~2,050,000 units in US (plus 250,000 in Canada, 21,000 in Mexico)
hazardSummary: A defective crimped wire connector within the internal heating assembly can overheat, melt surrounding plastic casing, catch fire, or cause severe contact burns during normal cooking cycles.
batchCodes: All manufacturing batches manufactured prior to December 2022. Model number is printed on the bottom rating label.
incidentsReported: 205 consumer reports of air fryers catching fire, burning, melting, overheating, or smoking, including 10 reports of minor superficial burns.
consumerAction: Immediately stop using the recalled air fryers. Unplug from electrical socket. Cut the power cord off at the base, write your initials on the label, and register at the official Cosori recall portal for a free replacement air fryer or alternate product.
chemicalRisk: None (mechanical crimp electrical resistance failure; toxic thermal off-gassing occurs when casing melts)
verificationTip: Look on the bottom underside label of the air fryer under 'Model:'. If the model starts with CP158, CP137, CP258, CAF-P581, or CS158, it is covered under this recall.

productName: BlendJet 2 Portable Cordless Blenders
hazardSummary: The lithium-ion battery base can overheat or catch fire during charging or operation, and the stainless steel blender blades can break off during blending, leaving metal shards in consumer drinks and smoothies.
modelNumbers: BlendJet 2 (Serial numbers with first 4 digits between 5201 and 5542)
batchCodes: Units with serial numbers beginning with four digits from 5201 through 5542 printed on the bottom base.
incidentsReported: 329 reports of blender blades breaking during use; 17 reports of fire or overheating resulting in property damage exceeding $150,000; 49 burn injuries and 1 laceration injury.
consumerAction: Immediately stop using the recalled blenders. Remove the silicone base seal gasket, cut the rubber seal into 3 pieces, photograph the cut seal and serial number, and submit to BlendJet for a free replacement base unit.
chemicalRisk: Lithium-ion battery thermal runaway risk and metal fragmentation in consumable food products
verificationTip: Invert the blender and inspect the bottom. Locate the embossed serial number. If the first 4 digits are between 5201 and 5542, your unit is recalled.

productName: Crock-Pot 6-Quart Express Crock Multi-Cookers
hazardSummary: The multi-cooker can pressurize if the lid is not fully locked in place. When the user attempts to open the lid under pressure, the lid can suddenly detach, violently ejecting scalding food and boiling liquid.
batchCodes: Date codes K160TS through K365TS and L001TS through L273TS engraved on one of the prongs of the electric plug and bottom rating label.
incidentsReported: 119 reports of lid detachment while pressurized, resulting in 99 burn injuries ranging in severity from first-degree to third-degree burns.
consumerAction: Immediately stop using the product in pressure cooking mode. Consumers may continue using for slow cooking and sautéing. Contact Sunbeam for a free upgraded replacement lid.
chemicalRisk: None (mechanical locking bayonet lug tolerance defect)
verificationTip: Look on the bottom label for model number SCCPPC600-V1. Then inspect the electrical plug prongs for date codes starting with 'K' or 'L'.

productName: Cupkin Double-Walled Stainless Steel Children's Cups (8 oz & 16 oz)
hazardSummary: The vacuum sealing dot located on the bottom base of the cup contains high concentrations of lead that exceed the federal lead content ban under the Consumer Product Safety Improvement Act (CPSIA). If the bottom base cap drops or detaches, children are exposed to toxic lead.
batchCodes: All color variations (12 solid colors and paired sets) sold from January 2018 through March 2023.
incidentsReported: Zero injuries reported prior to recall; initiated following independent laboratory XRF lead testing indicating lead levels exceeding 1,000 ppm at the sealing bead.
consumerAction: Immediately take the cups away from children and cease using them. Visit Cupkin's recall claim page to submit photographic proof of the cups for a 100% full refund.
chemicalRisk: Lead exceeds 90 ppm CPSIA federal limit. Lead is a neurotoxin that causes developmental delay and neurological toxicity in infants and young children.
verificationTip: Check the cup bottom for the embossed 'Cupkin' logo. All 8 oz and 16 oz stainless steel double-walled cups sold on Amazon prior to March 2023 are affected.

productName: Bindle Bottle 2-in-1 Vacuum-Insulated Water Bottles (13, 20, 24 & 32 oz)
hazardSummary: The bottom unscrewable storage compartment contains an exposed lead solder bead at the bottom of the vacuum seal. In addition, the storage compartment lid seal tested positive for Bisphenol A (BPA), which can leach into snacks stored inside.
batchCodes: All bottles manufactured and sold between December 2018 and February 2023.
incidentsReported: No direct illnesses reported; recall initiated after consumer advocacy testing detected exposed unencapsulated lead solder inside the dry storage chamber.
consumerAction: Immediately stop using the bottom storage compartment of the bottle. Do not place food, snacks, or medicine in the lower container. Contact Bindle Bottle for a free repair kit containing a silicone cover seal.
contactInfo: Bindle Bottle Recall Hotline: 1-888-551-2221 (Mon-Fri 9am-5pm PT) | bindlebottle.com/pages/recall
chemicalRisk: Lead solder dot in direct proximity to stored snacks. Lead is toxic if ingested and poses severe neurological harm.
verificationTip: Unscrew the bottom storage compartment and look at the circular center point. If you see a bare metallic dot or unsealed solder bead, it contains lead.

productName: Insignia Digital & Analog Air Fryers and Air Fryer Ovens
unitsAffected: ~970,000 units in US (plus 380,000 in Canada across both recalls)
hazardSummary: Internal heating elements and wire connections can overheat and fail to regulate temperature, causing handles to melt, glass viewing doors to shatter, and units to ignite.
batchCodes: All date codes for affected model numbers sold at Best Buy and on Amazon from November 2018 through November 2023.
incidentsReported: 137 reports in US and Canada of the air fryers catching fire, melting, or burning, including 10 property damage reports and 2 minor burn injuries.
consumerAction: Immediately stop using the air fryers. Unplug the unit. Visit Best Buy's recall support page or return the unit for a Best Buy gift card or check equal to the purchase price (minimum $50).
contactInfo: Best Buy Recall Support: 1-800-566-7498 (Mon-Fri 7am-6pm CT) | bestbuy.com/insigniaairfryerrecall
chemicalRisk: Plastic housing pyrolysis off-gassing and broken soda-lime glass projectile risks
verificationTip: Look on the bottom rating label for the INSIGNIA brand name and model numbers starting with 'NS-AF'.

productName: Cuisinart Food Processors with Riveted Stainless Steel S-Blades
hazardSummary: The riveted stainless steel chopper blades have four metal rivets joining the blades to the plastic hub. Over time and under dishwashing stress, the rivets fail and blade sections crack off into processed food, posing serious mouth laceration and tooth fracture hazards.
batchCodes: Only blades with four rivets attaching the stainless steel blades to the central beige plastic hub are recalled. Unriveted single-piece molded blades are NOT affected.
incidentsReported: 69 reports of consumers finding broken blade pieces in processed food, including 30 reports of mouth lacerations and tooth fractures.
consumerAction: Immediately stop using the riveted S-blade. Inspect your blade hub. If it has 4 rivets, contact Cuisinart to receive a free modern replacement blade assembly.
chemicalRisk: Mechanical metal ingestion hazard (acute laceration and puncture risks)
verificationTip: Look at the circular plastic center of your S-blade. If you see 4 round silver rivets holding the metal blades to the hub, do not use it.

productName: Lead-Glazed Artisan Ceramic Mugs, Bowls & Baking Dishes
unitsAffected: ~85,000 units across imported decorative kitchenware lines
hazardSummary: Imported rustic, hand-painted ceramic mugs, tajines, and baking dishes fired at low kiln temperatures contain traditional lead-fluxed glaze. When exposed to hot liquids (coffee, tea) or acidic ingredients (tomato sauce, citrus, vinegar), toxic lead and cadmium leach into food at levels 50x higher than FDA safety limits.
batchCodes: All ceramic tableware labeled 'For Decorative Use Only' or lacking verified FDA food-grade compliance documentation.
incidentsReported: Routine FDA border surveillance and California Department of Public Health sampling detected lead leaching up to 34.2 micrograms per milliliter (FDA threshold is 0.5 mcg/mL).
consumerAction: Immediately stop using rustic, low-fired imported earthenware ceramics for food or hot beverage preparation. Do not microwave or wash in the dishwasher, as heat accelerates glaze degradation.
contactInfo: FDA Food Safety Info: 1-888-SAFEFOOD | TJX Customer Service: 1-800-926-6299
chemicalRisk: Lead and cadmium toxic heavy metals cause neurotoxicity, renal tubular injury, and systemic toxicity.
verificationTip: Check the underside of ceramic mugs and platters. If you see rough unglazed terracotta, stamped 'Made in Mexico' or 'Traditional Artisan', test with a home lead swab (rhodizonate) before consuming hot liquids.

productName: Bella, Crux, and Cooks Multi-Function Electric Pressure Cookers
hazardSummary: The pressure cooker's lid lock mechanism can fail to engage or can unlock while the unit is still under high internal steam pressure, allowing the lid to fly open and eject boiling contents.
batchCodes: Units with date codes L15 to L20 printed on the rating label on the bottom of the base.
incidentsReported: 63 reports of lid unlocking under pressure, including 61 burn injuries, some involving second- and third-degree burns to the face, neck, and torso.
consumerAction: Immediately stop using the recalled pressure cookers. Contact Sensio for a full refund of purchase price.
chemicalRisk: Thermal kinetic energy burn trauma from boiling pressurized fat and water aerosols
verificationTip: Look on the bottom electrical rating label for the brand name (Bella, Crux, or Cooks) and model numbers 14467, 14567, 14721, 14737, or 22276.

productName: Tempered Soda-Lime Glass Bakeware Lids & Bowls
unitsAffected: ~1,500,000 units across affected commercial production runs
hazardSummary: Tempered soda-lime silicate glass bakeware lids and mixing bowls can shatter spontaneously or during sudden thermal shock (transfer from oven to cool countertop, or splashing cold liquid onto hot glass), projecting sharp high-velocity glass shards across the kitchen.
batchCodes: Soda-lime glass pieces manufactured with uppercase blue tint logo markings produced after 1998 borosilicate transition.
incidentsReported: Over 1,000 consumer complaints filed with CPSC SaferProducts.gov regarding sudden explosive shattering, with multiple lacerations and kitchen cleanup injuries.
consumerAction: Never place hot glass bakeware on wet or cold countertops. Always use a dry cloth or wooden trivet. If glass shows any visible chip, deep scratch, or cloudy stress crack, immediately discard it.
contactInfo: Instant Brands Customer Care: 1-800-828-7280 | Anchor Hocking: 1-877-376-9924
chemicalRisk: Mechanical laceration from razor-sharp high-stress tempered glass dice and projectile splinters
verificationTip: Look at the glass edge in natural daylight. Soda-lime glass displays a distinct greenish-blue tint. Borosilicate glass is virtually colorless or amber-tinted.

productName: Instant Pot 'Gem 65 8-in-1' Multicookers
hazardSummary: A manufacturing defect in the heating element can cause the unit to overheat, melt the plastic bottom base plate, and create a serious fire and electrical shock hazard.
batchCodes: Batch codes 1728, 1730, 1731, 1734, 1746 printed on the rating label on the bottom of the cooker base.
incidentsReported: 107 reports of overheating, with 5 reports of minor property damage due to melted bases. No injuries reported.
consumerAction: Immediately stop using the multicookers, unplug the unit, and contact Instant Brands for a free replacement multicooker base unit.
chemicalRisk: Thermal plastic degradation releasing toxic styrene and brominated flame retardant fumes
verificationTip: Inspect the silver rating label on the bottom of the base. Check for 'Gem 65 8-in-1' and a 4-digit batch code matching 1728, 1730, 1731, 1734, or 1746.

productName: Calphalon Contemporary Cutlery 8-Inch Carving & Slicing Knives
hazardSummary: The blade on the 8-inch carving and slicing knives can break during food preparation, posing a severe cut and laceration hazard to fingers and hands.
batchCodes: Knives sold individually and as part of 17-piece, 20-piece, and 21-piece Contemporary cutlery sets between September 2008 and December 2016.
incidentsReported: 3,150 reports of broken knives, including 27 consumer injuries involving cuts that required stitches.
consumerAction: Immediately stop using the recalled knives and contact Calphalon for an upgraded replacement knife.
chemicalRisk: None (metal fatigue and structural embrittlement along the knife heel and bolster)
verificationTip: Look on the blade face. Recalled knives are etched with 'Calphalon Contemporary' and model number KNR0008C or KNR1008C.

productName: Secura 5.3-Quart Electric Air Fryers
hazardSummary: A wire connection in the air fryer can overheat, posing fire and burn hazards during standard countertop cooking operations.
batchCodes: Units with date code 1901 and 1903 on the bottom rating label.
incidentsReported: 9 reports of the air fryers catching fire, burning, and smoking. No injuries or property damage reported.
consumerAction: Immediately stop using the recalled air fryers, unplug the appliance, cut the power cord, and submit photos to Secura for a $45 Amazon gift card or replacement Secura product.
chemicalRisk: Countertop electrical arc ignition and plastic melting off-gassing
verificationTip: Locate the silver label on the bottom of the unit. Check for model SAF-53D or SAF-53 with date codes 1901 or 1903.

productName: Contigo Kids Clean Motion Water Bottles (13, 14 & 20 oz)
unitsAffected: ~5,700,000 units in US (plus 157,000 in Canada, 28,000 in Mexico)
hazardSummary: The water bottle's clear silicone spout can detach during biting or drinking, posing a severe choking hazard to infants and young children.
modelNumbers: Contigo Kids Clean Motion (Black Spout Base)
batchCodes: Only bottles with a black spout base and clear silicone sprout cover are recalled.
incidentsReported: 427 reports of the silicone spout detaching, including 27 instances where a child found the detached spout in their mouth.
consumerAction: Immediately take the water bottles away from children. Inspect the spout. If the spout base beneath the clear silicone is black, contact Contigo for a free replacement lid assembly.
chemicalRisk: Mechanical obstruction of airway; silicone itself is food-grade inert
verificationTip: Look at the pop-up drinking spout. If the base piece directly beneath the transparent silicone spout is BLACK, it is recalled. (New safe lids have a colored spout base).

productName: Pillowfort Children's Plastic Plates, Bowls & Cups
hazardSummary: The polypropylene plastic tableware can crack, peel, or break into sharp shards when heated in the microwave or dropped, creating choking and cut hazards for children.
batchCodes: Sold in sets of 6 and individual units in colors pink, green, yellow, blue, peach, and mint from June 2021 through January 2023.
incidentsReported: 19 reports of plastic cracking or peeling, including 2 reports of children cutting their hands or mouth on broken plastic fragments.
consumerAction: Immediately take the recalled tableware away from children and return them to any Target store for a full refund in the form of a Target GiftCard.
chemicalRisk: Polypropylene structural brittleness under microwave thermal excitation
verificationTip: Turn the plate or bowl upside down and check for the embossed 'Pillowfort' brand name along with 'Made in China'.

productName: Wilton Recipe Right Non-Stick Baking & Roasting Pans
hazardSummary: Under high oven temperatures (exceeding 400°F / 204°C), defective batches of silicone-polyester non-stick coating blister and peel off in sheets, adhering to baked goods and exposing raw steel beneath.
batchCodes: Production date stamps 2019-Q3 and 2020-Q1 stamped on retail cardboard sleeves.
incidentsReported: Over 240 consumer reports of gray coating flakes adhering to brownies, cakes, and cookies. No acute poisoning recorded.
consumerAction: Stop baking with pans exhibiting bubbling, blistered, or peeling coating. Do not scrape flakes into food. Contact Wilton for replacement warranty credit.
chemicalRisk: Synthetic silicone-polyester polymer flaking; ingestion of particulate non-stick resin
verificationTip: Look on the pan rim stamped underside for the 7-digit item number (e.g. 2105-962). Inspect corners for bubbling or peeling finish.

productName: Farberware Complete Portable Countertop Dishwashers
hazardSummary: The internal heating coil assembly can overheat and melt the plastic dishwasher wash tub, burning kitchen counters and igniting surrounding materials.
batchCodes: Units with serial numbers between 2021050001 and 2021111500.
incidentsReported: 8 reports of heating element melting the plastic housing, including 1 incident of cabinet scorch damage. No injuries reported.
consumerAction: Immediately stop using and unplug the recalled countertop dishwashers. Contact Farberware for a prepaid shipping label and full purchase refund.
chemicalRisk: Polymer degradation and electrical fire risk in wet high-humidity appliance environment
verificationTip: Check the rating plate on the rear panel of the dishwasher. Verify if the model number is FCP-DW01WH.

productName: Ninja Foodi Cold & Hot Blender Glass Pitchers
recallId: CPSC Safety Notice & Pitcher Replacement Program
hazardSummary: When heating soups at maximum temperatures, the glass pitcher base seal can fail under thermal expansion, causing boiling soup to leak into the motorized coupler or causing bottom glass micro-fractures.
batchCodes: Date codes 1932 through 2025 stamped on the metal prongs of the power plug.
incidentsReported: 52 reports of seal leakage or glass fracturing during hot soup cycle, with 6 minor scalding incidents.
consumerAction: Do not fill hot liquids beyond the 56 oz 'Max Hot Liquid' line. Inspect the bottom heating base for hairline cracks. Contact SharkNinja for warranty replacement pitcher if leakage occurs.
chemicalRisk: None (thermal scalding and mechanical glass failure)
verificationTip: Look on the bottom underside of the glass pitcher or rating plate on the motor base for model HB152 or HB150.

productName: Primark Rustic Floral Ceramic Mug & Bowl Collections
unitsAffected: ~110,000 units across Europe and US stores
hazardSummary: Laboratory tests established that lead and cadmium leach from the decorative surface glaze into acidic beverages and soups at levels exceeding the European Commission Directive 84/500/EEC and FDA food contact safety thresholds.
batchCodes: Sold in Primark stores between August 2022 and January 2023.
incidentsReported: Detected during official customs market surveillance testing by health authorities.
consumerAction: Immediately cease using these ceramic mugs and bowls for food or hot drinks. Return them to any Primark store for an immediate no-receipt full refund.
chemicalRisk: Lead and cadmium leaching causes chronic toxic accumulation in kidneys, bones, and liver.
verificationTip: Inspect the base barcode sticker for Kimball number 6492801 or barcode starting with 5057581.

productName: The Pioneer Woman 6-Quart Portable Slow Cookers
hazardSummary: The lid clips can break or become dislodged when carrying the slow cooker, causing the lid to open unexpectedly and spilling hot contents, posing severe burn risks.
batchCodes: Series codes starting with letters 'C' or 'E' printed on the bottom metal base.
incidentsReported: 18 reports of lid clip failure resulting in spilled hot liquid, with 4 consumer second-degree burn reports.
consumerAction: Never carry the slow cooker by the lid handle while full of hot food. Contact Hamilton Beach for a free replacement locking clip kit and instructions.
contactInfo: Hamilton Beach Recall Support: 1-800-672-9240 (Mon-Fri 9am-4:30pm ET) | hamiltonbeach.com/recalls
chemicalRisk: None (kinetic mechanical failure of plastic latch under thermal load)
verificationTip: Look on the bottom of the base for model number 33062, 33063, 33064, or 33065, and inspect the side lid latch clips.
